samf-junior-2016-r2-02.title: Simplify
samf-junior-2016-r2-02.body:
The numerator is $13\cdot13\cdot12=2028$ and the denominator is $1+13+13+12=39=3\cdot13$. So the value is $\frac{13\cdot13\cdot12}{3\cdot13}=13\cdot4=52$.

**Answer: 52**

samf-junior-2016-r2-03.title: Count in front and behind
samf-junior-2016-r2-03.body:
There are $17$ people in front of Jess and $34$ behind her. With Jess herself: $17+1+34=52$.

**Answer: 52**

samf-junior-2016-r2-03.title: Overlap
samf-junior-2016-r2-03.body:
Counting from the front to Jess gives 18 people and from the back to Jess gives 35 people; Jess is counted twice, so $18+35-1=52$.

**Answer: 52**

samf-junior-2016-r2-04.title: Try the orders
samf-junior-2016-r2-04.body:
The six values of $p^q r$ are $2^3\cdot4=32$, $2^4\cdot3=48$, $3^2\cdot4=36$, $3^4\cdot2=162$, $4^2\cdot3=48$, $4^3\cdot2=128$. The largest is $162$.

**Answer: 162**

samf-junior-2016-r2-05.title: Isosceles triangle
samf-junior-2016-r2-05.body:
Each interior angle of the pentagon is $180^\circ-72^\circ=108^\circ$. Triangle $BCD$ has $BC=CD$, so it is isosceles with apex angle $\angle BCD=108^\circ$ and $x=\frac12(180^\circ-108^\circ)=36^\circ$.

**Answer: 36**

samf-junior-2016-r2-06.title: Subtract grey from total
samf-junior-2016-r2-06.body:
Case $n$ is an $(n+2)\times(n+2)$ grid whose central $n\times n$ block is grey. White squares: $(n+2)^2-n^2=4n+4$. For $n=10$ this is $44$.

**Answer: 44**

samf-junior-2016-r2-06.title: Count the border
samf-junior-2016-r2-06.body:
Case 10 has a $10\times10$ grey centre. The white border has two strips of $10$ (top and bottom) and two strips of $12$ (left and right, including corners): $20+24=44$.

**Answer: 44**

samf-junior-2016-r2-07.title: Pair the terms
samf-junior-2016-r2-07.body:
Pair each even number with the odd number just before it: $(2-1)+(4-3)+\dots+(200-199)$. There are $100$ pairs, each equal to $1$, so the total is $100$.

**Answer: 100**

samf-junior-2016-r2-08.title: Angle sums
samf-junior-2016-r2-08.body:
The square has one vertex on the base. The angles between the base and the two sides of the square at that vertex are $a$ and $b$, and $a+b=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$. The two base angles of the equilateral triangle are $60^\circ$. The two small triangles at the base corners have angle sums $x+a+60=180$ and $y+b+60=180$. Adding: $x+y+(a+b)=240$, so $x+y=240-90=150$.

**Answer: 150**

samf-junior-2016-r2-09.title: Zero must be included
samf-junior-2016-r2-09.body:
Suppose none of the four integers is $0$ and the product equals one of them, $m$. Dividing by $m$, the other three integers (distinct and nonzero) would have product $1$, which would force all three to be $\pm1$, impossible. So one of the integers is $0$; then the product is $0$, which equals that integer. The possible quadruples are $-3,\dots,0$; $-2,\dots,1$; $-1,\dots,2$; $0,\dots,3$. The largest integer that can occur is $3$.

**Answer: 3**

samf-junior-2016-r2-10.title: Factorise
samf-junior-2016-r2-10.body:
$2016=2^5\cdot3^2\cdot7$. Odd factors are the factors of $3^2\cdot7=63$. The largest is $63$, the second largest is $63/3=21$. Difference $=42$.

**Answer: 42**

samf-junior-2016-r2-11.title: Pick a convenient number
samf-junior-2016-r2-11.body:
Take $200$ girls and $100$ boys. Completed: $60+45=105$ of $300$. Still to do: $195$ of $300=65\%$.

**Answer: 65**

samf-junior-2016-r2-12.title: Use the base EC
samf-junior-2016-r2-12.body:
$EC=\frac35BC$. Triangle $DEC$ has base $EC$ and height $DC$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot\frac35BC\cdot DC=\frac3{10}[ABCD]=9$. Hence $[ABCD]=30$.

**Answer: 30**

samf-junior-2016-r2-13.title: Units
samf-junior-2016-r2-13.body:
Let the remaining distance be $1$ unit. He slept for $2$ units. After waking he still has $1$ unit; he had been awake for half the journey, so $2+1=3$ units are the second half and the whole journey is $6$ units. He slept $\frac26=\frac13$ of the journey, so $n=3$.

**Answer: 3**

samf-junior-2016-r2-14.title: Compare with the number
samf-junior-2016-r2-14.body:
I got $40\%$ of the number instead of $160\%$. To go from $40\%$ to $160\%$ I multiply by $4$, i.e. an increase of $300\%$.

**Answer: 300**

samf-junior-2016-r2-15.title: Total ages
samf-junior-2016-r2-15.body:
Two years ago the ages summed to $4\times19=76$. The four members have gained $2$ years each: $76+8=84$ now. With the child the sum is $5\times19=95$. The child is $95-84=11$.

**Answer: 11**

samf-junior-2016-r2-16.title: Count the wins
samf-junior-2016-r2-16.body:
There are $\binom42=6$ games, so $6$ wins in total. Let $A,B,C$ each have $w$ wins and $D$ have $d$ wins: $3w+d=6$. Since $A$ beat $D$, $d\le2$, so $d=0$ with $w=2$ (the only possibility, because $d\in\{0,3,6\}$ for $3w+d=6$ and $d\le 2$). An example: $A$ beats $B,D$; $B$ beats $C,D$; $C$ beats $A,D$.

**Answer: 0**

samf-junior-2016-r2-17.title: Both factors same sign
samf-junior-2016-r2-17.body:
The product is positive when both factors are positive ($n>38$) or both negative ($n<8$). $n=1,\dots,7$ gives $7$ values and $n=39,\dots,49$ gives $11$ values. Total $18$.

**Answer: 18**

samf-junior-2016-r2-18.title: Split the shaded region
samf-junior-2016-r2-18.body:
The midpoints cut $ABC$ into four equal triangles. The line $AG$ passes through the midpoint $H$ of $DE$, so the part of the shaded region inside $ADE$ is triangle $AHE$, half of $ADE$: $\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac18$ of $ABC$.

The rest of the shaded region lies inside triangle $DEF$, whose centre is also $G$. The lines $GA$, $GB$, $GC$ pass through the midpoints of the sides of $DEF$ and cut it into three congruent quadrilaterals; the shaded part $EHGI$ is one of them, so it is $\frac13\cdot\frac14=\frac1{12}$ of $ABC$.

Total: $\frac18+\frac1{12}=\frac5{24}$ of $120$, which is $25$.

**Answer: 25**

samf-junior-2016-r2-19.title: Fraction of the circle
samf-junior-2016-r2-19.body:
The radius is $3$ cm, so the circle has area $9\pi$. The unshaded area is $9\pi-7\pi=2\pi$, which is $\frac29$ of the circle. The unshaded regions are the two equal sectors at the top left and bottom right, so each has a central angle of $\frac12\cdot\frac29\cdot360^\circ=40^\circ$.

The triangle formed by the centre $O$, $B$ and $C$ is isosceles ($OB=OC$) with apex angle $40^\circ$, so $x=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}2=70^\circ$.

**Answer: 70**

samf-junior-2016-r2-20.title: Count by hundreds and units
samf-junior-2016-r2-20.body:
Choose the hundreds digit $h\in\{1,\dots,9\}$ and units digit $u>h$: there are $9-h$ choices for $u$, and the tens digit is free ($10$ choices). Total: $10\sum_{h=1}^{9}(9-h)=10(8+7+\dots+0)=10\cdot36=360$.

**Answer: 360**
